clue.text: Rebellious sets in a Home Counties town

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse to stay in line, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unruly television sets cause trouble in a commuter town near London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebellious' reshuffles SETSINA. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; Staines is a Thames-side town in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey commuter town on the Thames, so a town in the Home Counties around London.

clue.text: People giving direction to youngsters

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass direction
mites are small children

explanation.surface: Adults are telling children which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of peoples descended, by tradition, from Shem, such as Arabs and Jews.

clue.text: A piece for the odd recital

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange happened to the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician plays one item for a rather strange concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper item or written report is a piece of writing.

clue.text: In general there's clean air, naturally, in Scotland

indicators.note: there is, meaning the word is present inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: Fresh, natural air is generally to be found up in the Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'cleaN AIR Naturally'. 'in Scotland' defines loosely: the answer is a town on the Moray Firth.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town and former county on the Moray Firth, so a place in Scotland.

clue.text: "Newton, childlike sage! reader of the works of God." Cowper (The Task)

definitions.text: "Newton, childlike sage! reader of the works of God." Cowper (The Task)

parts.words: "Newton, childlike sage! reader of the works of God." Cowper (The Task)
parts.note: a quotation with its adjective cut out: in William Cowper's poem the scientist is praised as a wise, shrewd reader of the works of God

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the missing word in Cowper's line from The Task stands before 'reader'. Its sense of wise insight is hinted at by 'sage' just before.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise and shrewd in judgement, the word Cowper chose to praise the scientist Newton.

clue.text: The chorus don't

definitions.meaning: the repeated lines sung after each verse of a song
as a verb, to hold back from doing something, as in 'please don't smoke'

explanation.definitionFit: A song's recurring burden is its chorus, and to abstain from doing something is a polite way of saying don't.

clue.text: Check about exercise, being over 50

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit over the later one

parts.note: re means about or concerning
PE is physical education
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A doctor checks on someone's exercise now they are past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being over' says RE and PE stand above L in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to check it, driving the attacker back.

clue.text: A member of society seen from a new position

indicators.note: the letters are placed into a new position, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A socialite is seen in a fresh light from a different viewpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new position' rearranges SEEN FROM A.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Freemasons, a fraternal secret society.

clue.text: Keeping so many is a little daunting

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the phrase for 'a little' keeps the others inside it

parts.note: a wee is Scots for a little
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Looking after so many children is rather intimidating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' puts SO and M inside A WEE: A WE(SOM)E. 'Wee', Scots for small, is a standard crossword word for little.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awe-inspiring is so overwhelming it can be intimidating and daunting.

clue.text: An unusual perfume that's now in process of production

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the short word is rearranged

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: A novel fragrance is just being developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfume' could be read as the definition, but the definition is the long phrase at the end; 'unusual' only rearranges the little word An.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, still emerging and developing.

clue.text: Floor-covering getting in a mess?

definitions.meaning: woven material laid on a floor, like rush mats
becoming tangled, as hair or fur does when it clumps

explanation.definitionFit: Coarse woven mats laid as a floor covering, and also the present participle of hair tangling into knots.

clue.text: Likes the page with adverts

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for page
to advert to something is to mention or allude to it, so adverts means refers

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys the newspaper page that carries the advertisements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adverts' looks like the noun for advertisements, but it is the verb: to advert to a subject is to refer to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prefers something likes it more than the alternatives, a near synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Practical latch-nice change, that

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the hyphenated pair

explanation.surface: A handyman proposes swapping a nice latch for a better door catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges the nine letters of LATCH-NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical skill concerns the hands-on, applied side of a craft, the practical rather than the theoretical side.

clue.text: A beast's low and heartless girl

parts.note: to low is to make the deep sound of cattle, a moo

indicators.note: removing the heart means taking out the middle letter of the girl's name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cow lows mournfully while a cold-hearted girl looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes U, the middle of SUE, leaving SE. The 's of 'beast's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large antlered deer of northern forests, so certainly a beast.

clue.text: Drop off skins on return

indicators.note: on its way back the word for skins is read from right to left

parts.note: peels are the skins of fruit

explanation.surface: Fruit skins are dropped in the bin on the way home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to nod off, to fall into slumber.

clue.text: Declare the head should hold back alcoholic drink

indicators.note: to hold is to contain the other piece inside

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: the drink is written backwards

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A headteacher announces that someone should hold back on the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the cider into REDIC; 'pate' is an old jokey word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate something is to state or assert it, to declare it to be so.

clue.text: Didn't keep to the budget-even sport's affected

indicators.note: affected suggests the letters have been altered or disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A sports club blows its budget even on minor games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges the letters of EVEN SPORT (the 's is no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Spending beyond the funds allowed is failing to keep within a budget.

clue.text: Writing in French, scoff about a struggle

parts.note: writing the word 'in' in French gives 'en'

indicators.note: about means around, so the scoffing word goes round the A

parts.note: to scoff food is to devour it

explanation.surface: A writer in French complains, mocking a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing in French' asks for the French word for 'in'; 'about' wraps the scoffing word round the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an effort or attempt, a striving or struggle to achieve something.

clue.text: Checked journals sitting amid the tall grass

indicators.note: one thing sitting amid another goes inside it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of marshes
the press is newspapers and journals collectively

explanation.surface: Magazines lie hidden among long grass where someone stopped to read them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked' could be ticked off, but here it means held back, as feelings are.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked emotions are held back or restrained, which is what repressed means.

clue.text: Athletes managers

definitions.meaning: people who run a business, as in 'runs the shop'

explanation.definitionFit: Racers on a track are competitors who run, and those who run organisations are their bosses.

clue.text: One in support is to lay the groundwork

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of the other

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supporter is preparing the foundations.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to be first to develop it, preparing the way for others.

clue.text: The opener very often exhibits great resolution

indicators.note: exhibits says the answer is on show inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A cricket opening batsman often shows real determination at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'opeNER VEry'. In cricket the opener is the first batsman in, who must face the fresh fast bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and steadiness under pressure, a strong resolve, is what having the nerve means.

clue.text: Delighted leftist getting a blow in

indicators.note: the blow gets in, inside the leftist

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger
a gale is a strong blow of wind

explanation.surface: A left-winger is thrilled to land a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leftist' is the colour long associated with socialism and communism; 'getting ... in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain or delight them, often with stories.

clue.text: Oriental arranging one flower in quarters

indicators.note: the flower is placed in the middle of the two quarters

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are two quarters of the compass
an aster is a flower, a Michaelmas daisy

explanation.surface: An Asian florist arranges a single bloom in each part of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ASTER between E and N, two compass quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things of the East, eastern parts of the world.

clue.text: Ruthless she certainly was not!

parts.note: read Ruth-less: the woman in the Book of Ruth who was never without her loyal daughter-in-law Ruth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruthless' looks like 'merciless', but split it as Ruth-less: in the Bible Ruth refused to leave her mother-in-law, saying 'whither thou goest, I will go'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament widow whom her daughter-in-law Ruth followed to Bethlehem, so she was never without Ruth.

clue.text: Guides provided by the way

parts.note: 'by the way' looks like 'incidentally' but means literally at the roadside, where directions are posted

explanation.definitionFit: Signposts at the roadside direct travellers, guidance placed beside the road.

clue.text: Call up the right associate

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: Someone phones a right-wing colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally troops is to summon or call them up to assemble.

clue.text: Cook's new mates

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the word's letters

explanation.surface: A chef has some new friends in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MATES; the 's of 'Cook's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook vegetables over boiling water is to steam them.

clue.text: Are you old-fashioned, reflective, all a viewer should be?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the archaic phrase is turned round

parts.note: in archaic English 'are you' is 'be ye'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quizzer asks whether you are old-fashioned and thoughtful, as any viewer ought to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are you' in archaic English is 'be ye'; 'reflective' turns that round to EYEB.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe of the eye is the organ through which we see, so a viewer in the literal sense.

clue.text: Tell too many stories to be on top

definitions.meaning: to lie excessively, telling stories meaning fibbing
to rest over something else, as one layer of rock on another

explanation.definitionFit: Read as over plus lie it means fibbing to excess; as one word it means resting upon another layer.

clue.text: Filled with regret about the Church, but only for a spell

indicators.note: the word for regret is filled with the church letters, holding them in its middle

parts.note: to be sorry is to feel regret
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone briefly feels remorse over the church, but the feeling soon passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but only for a spell' pretends to mean briefly; the spell is a magical one, and 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Witchcraft and enchantment are worked by casting a magic spell.

clue.text: Managed to hold the first man back, being fast

indicators.note: one word is made to hold another inside it

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so managed is ran

indicators.note: the name is written backwards

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man

explanation.surface: A manager restrains the leading man at the back, determined to hold firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the first man into MADA; 'being fast' looks like speed but means abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim holy month of daytime abstinence from food and drink, a religious fast.
